q: Mechanisms of breathing are for _____ which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of carbon dioxide from the body.
e: Mechanisms of breathing are for gas exchange which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of carbon dioxide from the body. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Circulation is not gas exchange.

q: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient _____ to exchange gases for the whole organism.
e: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient surface area to exchange gases for the whole organism. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Mass is not surface area.

q: Aquatic animals that use gills include polychaetes, crustaceans, sea stars and fish, whereas aquatic turtles use _____ for gas exchange.
e: Aquatic animals that use gills include polychaetes, crustaceans, sea stars and fish, whereas aquatic turtles use cloaca for gas exchange. Some vertebrates share a cloaca for digestive, urinary, and reproductive openings. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Gills is different: gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals.

q: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called _____.
e: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called lamellae. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Tracheae is not lamellae.

q: The _____ flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a capillary.
e: The counter current flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a capillary. Counter-current flow in fish gills keeps a gradient so more oxygen is extracted. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin. Cross is not counter current.

q: Some terrestrial animals use tracheae for breathing, such as _____.
e: Some terrestrial animals use tracheae for breathing, such as insects. Many insects breathe through a tracheal system, not lungs. Spiders is not insects.

q: Spiders and scorpions use _____ for breathing.
e: Spiders and scorpions use book lungs for breathing. Book lungs are stacked gas-exchange plates in some arachnids. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Gills is different: gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals.

q: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the _____ for gas exchange.
e: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the buccal cavity for gas exchange. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Intestine is not buccal cavity.

q: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the _____.
e: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the diaphragm. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Pericardium is not diaphragm.

q: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called _____ muscles.
e: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called intercostal muscles. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Abdominal is not intercostal.

q: The trachea splits into two tubes called the _____, one leading to each lung.
e: The trachea splits into two tubes called the bronchi, one leading to each lung. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Bronchioles is different: bronchioles are the finer airways that end in alveoli.

q: Each bronchus divides into smaller tubes called bronchioles, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs called _____.
e: Each bronchus divides into smaller tubes called bronchioles, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs called alveoli. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases. Bronchioles are the finer airways that end in alveoli. Glomeruli is not alveoli.

q: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of _____ which support the airway and keep them open.
e: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of gristle or cartilage which support the airway and keep them open. Cartilage keeps airways such as the trachea open. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Bone is not gristle or cartilage.

q: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the _____ membranes.
e: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the pleural membranes. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Synovial is not pleural.

q: Between the two pleural membranes is a space filled with a thin layer of liquid called _____ fluid.
e: Between the two pleural membranes is a space filled with a thin layer of liquid called pleural fluid. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Serous is not pleural.

q: Some cells in the lining of trachea and bronchi secrete _____ which traps particles of dirt or bacteria.
e: Some cells in the lining of trachea and bronchi secrete mucus which traps particles of dirt or bacteria. Mucus traps particles; cilia sweep that dirt away from the lungs. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Bile is not mucus.

q: _____ on cells lining the trachea and bronchi prevent the mucus and trapped particles from entering the lungs by beating and sweeping.
e: Cilia on cells lining the trachea and bronchi prevent the mucus and trapped particles from entering the lungs by beating and sweeping. Cilia are tiny beating hairs that move mucus and trapped dust. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Flagella is not Cilia.

q: During inhalation, the external intercostal muscles _____ and the internal intercostal muscles relax.
e: During inhalation, the external intercostal muscles contract and the internal intercostal muscles relax. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing. Tear is not contract.

q: During inhalation, the muscles of diaphragm contract and the diaphragm becomes _____.
e: During inhalation, the muscles of diaphragm contract and the diaphragm becomes flattened. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Domed is not flattened.

q: During exhalation, the chest _____ in volume and increases in pressure.
e: During exhalation, the chest decreases in volume and increases in pressure. Remains same is not decreases.

q: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an _____ cavity.
e: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an airtight cavity. Ventilation is moving air or water across the gas-exchange surface. Porous is not airtight.

q: The conditions for gas exchange vary depending on whether the breathing medium is air or _____.
e: The conditions for gas exchange vary depending on whether the breathing medium is air or water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Soil is not water.

q: Respiratory organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available _____ for gas exchange.
e: Respiratory organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available surface area for gas exchange. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Weight is not surface area.

q: Marine worms of the phylum Annelida called _____ use gills for gas exchange.
e: Marine worms of the phylum Annelida called polychaetes use gills for gas exchange. Many polychaete worms use gills in water. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Nematodes is not polychaetes.

q: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up _____ from the water.
e: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up oxygen from the water. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin. Carbon dioxide is different: carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: The diffusion of gases takes place from an area of higher concentration to an area of _____ concentration.
e: The diffusion of gases takes place from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Equal is not lower.

q: Most organisms obtain their energy from the oxidation of food in a process known as cell _____.
e: Most organisms obtain their energy from the oxidation of food in a process known as cell respiration. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Food chains show how chemical energy flows from producers to consumers. Digestion is not respiration.

q: The rate of gas exchange is affected by the area, distance, concentration gradient, and the _____ with which molecules diffuse through membranes.
e: The rate of gas exchange is affected by the area, distance, concentration gradient, and the speed with which molecules diffuse through membranes. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Color is not speed.

q: Efficient gas exchange systems must have a large surface area to _____ ratio.
e: Efficient gas exchange systems must have a large surface area to volume ratio. As an animal grows, volume rises faster than surface, so simple skin exchange is not enough. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Weight is not volume.

q: In daylight, when photosynthesis is going on in green plants, they take in carbon dioxide and give out _____.
e: In daylight, when photosynthesis is going on in green plants, they take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Nitrogen is different: nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: In plants, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through the stomata and the _____.
e: In plants, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through the stomata and the lenticels. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases. Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through stomata. Roots is different: roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low.

q: A stoma is bounded by a pair of specialized cells known as the _____ cells which contain chloroplasts.
e: A stoma is bounded by a pair of specialized cells known as the guard cells which contain chloroplasts. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Epidermal is not guard.

q: Stomatal opening and closing depends on changes in the _____ pressure of the guard cells.
e: Stomatal opening and closing depends on changes in the turgor pressure of the guard cells. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. Atmospheric is not turgor.

q: Lenticels are small openings on stems, fruits, tubers and roots that allow the passage of _____.
e: Lenticels are small openings on stems, fruits, tubers and roots that allow the passage of air. Air of the atmosphere supplies oxygen and carbon dioxide for life. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases. Water is different: water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.

q: The two human lungs contain about _____ millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli.
e: The two human lungs contain about seven hundred millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli. Older schemes listed seven ranks; adding domain makes eight. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases.

q: The total surface area of alveoli in the two human lungs is about _____ $m^2$.
e: The total surface area of alveoli in the two human lungs is about 60 m^2. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases. 100 is not 60.

q: The blood is separated from the air inside each alveolus by only _____ cell layers.
e: The blood is separated from the air inside each alveolus by only two cell layers. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Each alveolus is a thin-walled sac where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse. Four is different: four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.

q: In humans, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the pulmonary _____.
e: In humans, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Capillary is not artery.

q: The capillaries carrying oxygenated blood from the alveoli join up to form the pulmonary vein, which returns blood to the left _____ of the heart.
e: The capillaries carrying oxygenated blood from the alveoli join up to form the pulmonary vein, which returns blood to the left atrium of the heart. An atrium is an upper heart chamber that receives blood. The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from lungs to the heart. Ventricle is not atrium.

q: In insects, the _____ which are the finest branches extend close to the surface of nearly every cell.
e: In insects, the tracheoles which are the finest branches extend close to the surface of nearly every cell. Insect tracheoles take air almost to the tissues, so blood need not carry the gases. Many insects breathe through a tracheal system, not lungs. Lungs is different: lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Single-celled organisms and small and thin organisms rely on _____ for gas exchange.
e: Single-celled organisms and small and thin organisms rely on diffusion for gas exchange. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Osmosis is different: osmosis is diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane.

q: In many animals a blood _____ system carries gases to and from the gas exchange surface.
e: In many animals a blood circulatory system carries gases to and from the gas exchange surface. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Skeletal is not circulatory.

q: Efficient gas exchange systems must be _____ to gases.
e: Efficient gas exchange systems must be permeable to gases. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Impermeable is not permeable.

q: The energy plants need for all their living processes apart from photosynthesis comes from _____.
e: The energy plants need for all their living processes apart from photosynthesis comes from respiration. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Transpiration is different: transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata.

q: Water vapour is released into the atmosphere through stomatal pores during _____.
e: Water vapour is released into the atmosphere through stomatal pores during transpiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Germination is not transpiration.

q: In the daytime, water diffuses into guard cells by _____, increasing their turgor.
e: In the daytime, water diffuses into guard cells by osmosis, increasing their turgor. Osmosis is diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. Active transport is different: active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient.

q: Lenticels provide a pathway for direct exchange of gases between internal tissues and the _____.
e: Lenticels provide a pathway for direct exchange of gases between internal tissues and the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases. Water is different: water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.

q: Viewed through a microscope, alveoli look like bunches of grapes and are covered with tiny blood _____.
e: Viewed through a microscope, alveoli look like bunches of grapes and are covered with tiny blood capillaries. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens. A microscope magnifies a specimen so hidden cell detail can be seen. Veins is not capillaries.

q: The distance separating blood from air in the alveolus is less than a _____ of a millimeter.
e: The distance separating blood from air in the alveolus is less than a thousandth of a millimeter. Each alveolus is a thin-walled sac where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse. Hundredth is not thousandth.

q: In fish, oxygenated blood is distributed to respiring tissues all over the body directly from the _____.
e: In fish, oxygenated blood is distributed to respiring tissues all over the body directly from the gills. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Liver is different: the liver stores glycogen, makes bile, and handles many blood chemicals.

q: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a relatively constant _____ environment, even when the external environment is changing.
e: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a relatively constant internal environment, even when the external environment is changing. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Physical is different: biophysics uses physical laws; it is not the same as biochemistry.

q: In plants, extra water is removed by transpiration and _____.
e: In plants, extra water is removed by transpiration and guttation. Guttation pushes liquid water out of hydathodes when root pressure is high. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. Photosynthesis is different: photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: About 85-90% of water lost from a plant is lost by _____ transpiration.
e: About 85-90% of water lost from a plant is lost by stomatal transpiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. Cuticular is not stomatal.

q: Guttation is the expelling of excess water or nutrients through tiny openings called _____ on the tips or edges of leaves.
e: Guttation is the expelling of excess water or nutrients through tiny openings called hydathodes on the tips or edges of leaves. Guttation pushes liquid water out of hydathodes when root pressure is high. Stomata is different: stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

q: Padonmar kya ($Nelumbo$ $nucifera$) has _____ activities to maintain relatively stable tissue temperatures.
e: Padonmar kya (Nelumbo nucifera) has thermoregulation activities to maintain relatively stable tissue temperatures. Osmoregulation is different: osmoregulation controls water and solute balance.

q: In humans and other mammals, the core body temperature is monitored by a part of the brain called the thermoregulatory centre located in the _____.
e: In humans and other mammals, the core body temperature is monitored by a part of the brain called the thermoregulatory centre located in the hypothalamus. The hypothalamus is the brain centre that coordinates thermoregulation and much of homeostasis. Cerebrum is not hypothalamus.

q: When body temperature increases, arterioles leading to capillary loops in the dermis dilate in a process called _____.
e: When body temperature increases, arterioles leading to capillary loops in the dermis dilate in a process called vasodilation. Vasodilation widens skin arterioles so more heat can be lost. Vasoconstriction is not vasodilation.

q: When body temperature decreases, hairs are pulled upright by the contraction of hair _____ muscles to trap insulating air.
e: When body temperature decreases, hairs are pulled upright by the contraction of hair erector muscles to trap insulating air. Erector pili muscles lift hairs to trap an insulating layer of air. Hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys. Flexor is not erector.

q: Speeding up of body's metabolism and _____ are mechanisms that generate more heat when body temperature decreases.
e: Speeding up of body's metabolism and shivering are mechanisms that generate more heat when body temperature decreases. Shivering makes muscles release heat when the body is too cold. Vasodilation is different: vasodilation widens skin arterioles so more heat can be lost.

q: The liver stores excess glucose as _____ if the concentration in the blood gets too high.
e: The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen if the concentration in the blood gets too high. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

q: If the level of sugar in the blood falls, alpha cells of the Islet of Langerhans release a hormone called _____.
e: If the level of sugar in the blood falls, alpha cells of the Islet of Langerhans release a hormone called glucagon. Glucagon raises blood glucose by triggering glycogen breakdown in the liver. The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin and glucagon. Insulin is different: insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: If the concentration of blood sugar increases, insulin is released from _____ cells of the Islet of Langerhans.
e: If the concentration of blood sugar increases, insulin is released from beta cells of the Islet of Langerhans. The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin and glucagon. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar. Delta is not beta.

q: The human kidneys filter about _____ litres of blood per day and produce, on average, 1.5 litres of urine.
e: The human kidneys filter about 1,500 litres of blood per day and produce, on average, 1.5 litres of urine. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. 15 is not 1,500.

q: Each kidney consists of two regions; the outer region, the cortex and the inner region the _____.
e: Each kidney consists of two regions; the outer region, the cortex and the inner region the medulla. The medulla oblongata contains centres that help control breathing rate. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine. Pelvis is not medulla.

q: The pyramids in the kidney lead to a funnel-like structure called the _____ which connects with the ureter.
e: The pyramids in the kidney lead to a funnel-like structure called the pelvis which connects with the ureter. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine. The ureter carries urine from kidney to bladder. Bladder is different: the bladder stores urine until it is released.

q: A nephron consists of a glomerulus, a Bowman's capsule and a long renal _____.
e: A nephron consists of a glomerulus, a Bowman's capsule and a long renal tubule. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. Nephrons are the kidney's filtering and urine-forming units. Artery is not tubule.

q: Ultrafiltration forces fluid from the blood through the walls of the capillaries and the Bowman's capsule due to high blood _____ in the arteriole.
e: Ultrafiltration forces fluid from the blood through the walls of the capillaries and the Bowman's capsule due to high blood pressure in the arteriole. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens. Sugar is not pressure.

q: Selective reabsorption occurs in the tubule; the longer the loop of Henle, the greater the reabsorption of _____.
e: Selective reabsorption occurs in the tubule; the longer the loop of Henle, the greater the reabsorption of water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Urea is not water.

q: 'Antidiuresis' means producing less urine, controlled by the _____ hormone (ADH).
e: 'Antidiuresis' means producing less urine, controlled by the Antidiuretic hormone (ADH). Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water. Thyroxine is not Antidiuretic.

q: When the body loses too much water, ADH causes the collecting ducts to become more _____ to water.
e: When the body loses too much water, ADH causes the collecting ducts to become more permeable to water. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water. Rigid is not permeable.

q: Fruit ripening is one of the examples of a _____ biological feedback loop in plants.
e: Fruit ripening is one of the examples of a positive biological feedback loop in plants. Negative is not positive.

q: A ripe mango gives off a gas called _____ ($C_2H_4$) through its skin which signals neighbours to ripen.
e: A ripe mango gives off a gas called ethylene (C2H4) through its skin which signals neighbours to ripen. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: A baby suckling on the mother's nipple stimulates the pituitary gland to release prolactin and _____.
e: A baby suckling on the mother's nipple stimulates the pituitary gland to release prolactin and oxytocin. Oxytocin is a hypothalamic hormone involved in birth and milk ejection. Insulin is different: insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: Prolactin stimulates milk production, while oxytocin stimulates smooth muscles contraction allowing milk to _____.
e: Prolactin stimulates milk production, while oxytocin stimulates smooth muscles contraction allowing milk to eject. Oxytocin is a hypothalamic hormone involved in birth and milk ejection. Store is not eject.

q: Successful homeostasis and being able to maintain it in adverse conditions is one of the most important _____ advantages.
e: Successful homeostasis and being able to maintain it in adverse conditions is one of the most important evolutionary advantages. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits. Structural is not evolutionary.
